chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfaly, who linked it up to Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who mentioned from his forefathers (peace be upon them):

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote to his officials: Sharpen your pens, bring your lines close together, remove the superfluous from me, and aim for the essence of the meanings. Beware of excess, for the wealth of the Muslims cannot bear the harm [of waste].
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali instruct his officials to do to conserve resources in their correspondence?
ai.summary: This directive from Imam Ali (as) to his governors highlights the administrative principle of *ikhtisar* (brevity) and *iqtisad* (economy) in state correspondence, ensuring that public funds were not squandered on excessive paper and scribes. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s role as a model of efficient governance, where clarity of message takes precedence over ornamental verbosity to serve the *Bayt al-Mal* (public treasury) effectively.
